diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $q=\max_{1\leq i\leq\ell}|T_i|$, the joint distribution $\bbb{P}$ of the batch-sampling $\tau$
  can be represented by a $q$th-order tensor

issues.failure_explanation: In the row-paving batch-sampling of Example exampRowPaving, q equals the largest block size, so a draw tau whose effective set T_t has |T_t|<q necessarily contains repeated indices, and A_tau (S_tau) are the q-row matrices with repeated rows. Lemma lem6 defines beta^S_{i,j} as a max of ||S_tau A_tau||_2^2 over such q-tuples, which in general differs from ||S_{T_t}A_{T_t}||_2^2 (e.g. for T={1,2}, q=3, orthonormal rows, S=I: ||[a_1;a_1;a_2]||^2=2 while ||A_T||^2=1). Hence the proof's assertions beta^S_{i,j}=||S_{T_I(j)}A_{T_I(j)}||^2, B_{S;i}=B_S, and D^2 ⪰ S^T B_S^{-1} \hat P S are false: with T_1={1,2}, T_2={3}, q=3, orthonormal rows and symmetric probabilities over the preimage of T_1, one gets D^2_{11}=3p_1/4 while the claimed lower bound gives p_1. The same misidentification appears in (betaS_value) of Remark relaxOne, where beta^S of Corollary convRBSK_relaxed (a max over q-tuples with repeats) is equated with a max over effective sets, so the claimed exact recovery of the ND14 bound is unsupported for unequal pavings. The proof is only valid when all blocks have exactly q rows (and beta^S_{i,j} is read as a max over the support).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave and Remark relaxOne to pavings with all blocks of size q, or replace the Lemma lem6-based step by a direct argument: for a projection block, ||A_T^\dagger r_T||^2 = e^T A_T^\dagger A_T e ≥ e^T A_T^T S_T^2 A_T e / ||S_T A_T||_2^2, which yields D^2 ⪰ S^T B_S^{-1} \hat P S directly and then Lemma lem7 gives the stated bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave (and the prose promise that B_{S;i}^{-1} 'can be exactly described' for row pavings) is invalid for general (l,beta_Low,beta_Up) row pavings with unequal block sizes; the claims (betaS_value) and the recovery of Needell's bound in Remark relaxOne are unsupported in that case. The experimental setting (equal block sizes) is unaffected.
issues.title: Exact identification B_{S;i}=B_S fails for row pavings with unequal block sizes (repeated indices)
issues.why_classification: The stated bounds remain true but the given proof mechanism fails and must be replaced by a new contained argument (or the scope narrowed to equal-size blocks); no global architecture change, but more than a local typo fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, we focus on testing the bounds of the convergence rates provided by Theorems \ref{convRBSK_relaxed_pave} and \ref{convRBSK_sharper}

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion (thm4Eq2) is a deterministic inequality between population expectations, yet it is asserted 'with probability at least 1-delta' under a hypothesis on a finite random sample. The proof derives (thm4Eq8), a sample-average inequality valid only on a random event, and then 'takes expectation on both sides', which is not a valid inference (the inequality is not known to hold off that event, and expectation of sample means over a data-dependent conditioning does not yield the population expectations). Moreover Lemma lem5 is invoked for the pair (xi, ||x^{(k)}-x_*||_2^2) although the hypothesis only assumes nonnegative sample covariance of (xi, ||x^{(k)}-x_*||_2); nonnegative covariance with the norm does not imply it for the squared norm (e.g. centered xi=(-1,-1,1,1), y=(0,2,1,1)). What would actually be needed is E[xi_{tau^{(k-1)}}||x^{(k)}-x_*||^2] ≥ E[xi]E||x^{(k)}-x_*||^2, i.e. nonnegative population covariance, which fails generically and makes the stated bound false: take orthonormal rows a_1,a_2,a_3 in R^3, paving T_1={1,2}, T_2={3}, q=2, P(T_1)=0.9, P(T_2)=0.1, S=I, x^{(0)}-x_*=a_3. Then D^2=diag(0.9,0.9,0.1), E xi_tau = 2(0.9)(0.1)=0.18, E||x^{(1)}-x_*||^2=0.9, E||x^{(2)}-x_*||^2=0.81 > (1+epsilon-0.18)(0.9)=0.738+0.9 epsilon for any epsilon<0.08, while the sample-covariance hypothesis holds with positive probability (all samples draw T_1). Also E_k^{(j)} is undefined and the min over S in (thm4Eq2) presumes the hypotheses simultaneously for every S.

failure_location.quote: which holds with probability at least $1-\delta$. Since \(\tau\) and \(\tau^{(k-1)}\) follow the same distribution, we can replace \(\E[\xi_{\tau^{(k-1)}}]\) by \(\E[\xi_{\tau}]\). Taking expectation on both sides of (\ref{thm4Eq8}) leads to the sharper estimate (\ref{thm4Eq2}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the sample-covariance hypothesis by a verifiable population condition Cov(xi_{tau^{(k-1)}}, ||x^{(k)}-x_*||_2^2) ≥ 0 (or otherwise control E[xi ||e||^2] from below), under which E||x^{(k+1)}-x_*||^2 ≤ (1-E xi_tau) E||x^{(k)}-x_*||^2 follows directly without concentration, and must acknowledge that this condition fails in general (the counterexample above).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem convRBSK_sharper, the paper's headline 'sharper' concentration-based rate bound, is not established and is false as stated; all experimental comparisons of the 'Thm 4 bound' against ND14/GM21 and the abstract/conclusion claims of new tighter expected rate bounds derived via concentration inequalities rest on it.
issues.title: Concentration-based rate bound conflates sample and population quantities; conclusion false in general
issues.why_classification: The result is false as stated and the concentration/sample-based architecture cannot be patched; any valid version needs a different (population) hypothesis that excludes typical cases, so the advertised sharper expected-rate guarantee and the experiments built on it are lost.
